title: One finite quotient detects formal maps with a torsion comparison
statement: For X Noetherian and J an ideal, let b:Q→R be a coherent arrow whose kernel T is killed by a positive power of J. Suppose T→Q/J^(n+1)Q is monomorphic. For any coherent formal module M and formal maps f,g:M→Q^, equality f≫b^=g≫b^ and equality f_n=g_n at level n+1 imply f=g. Formal modules and completion are those of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module].

source.place: Tag 0889(1), affine comparison and uniqueness; Tags 05EK and 088A

proof.text: Write T = ker(b). For every m >= n, the separating map T -> Q/J^(n+1)Q factors through the quotient projection T -> T/J^(m+1)T. Monomorphy of the composite makes this projection mono; as a cokernel projection it is epi. In the abelian module category it is therefore an isomorphism. The quotient identities then make all transitions of the completion of T at and above n isomorphisms. This uses hsep directly; hker is not needed once hsep is assumed.

Coherent kernel closure makes T an object of CoherentModules X. The ordinary kernel fork lifts to a limiting kernel fork in this full subcategory by its universal property. Exactness of completion and the Mathlib exact-functor criterion imply preservation of finite limits, so its mapped kernel fork is limiting in the coherent formal category. Compatibility of preadditive structures uses Mathlib subsingleton_preadditive_of_hasBinaryBiproducts directly. Transport exactness along uniqueness of zero-morphism structures using congrArg₂ on the predicate quantifying over its zero-preservation witness; no duplicate auxiliary theorem is declared.

The comparison equality kills the composite of f-g with the completion of b. Lift f-g through the completed kernel fork. At n its composite with the completed inclusion is zero by hlevel. The inverse quotient projection of T identifies this equation with a zero composite with the separating map; cancel that mono and then the inverse quotient projection to make the factor at n zero.

For m >= n, naturality and cancellation of the invertible transition in completed T show that the factor at m is zero. For m < n, naturality and the epimorphic transition M_n -> M_m show it is zero. All coherent formal transitions are epimorphic by formalTransition_epi. Componentwise extensionality makes the factor zero; its kernel-factorization equation gives f-g=0 and hence f=g.

theorem formalMap_torsion_finite_detection
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (Q R : CoherentModules X) (b : Q ⟶ R)
    (hker : ∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
        (kernel b.hom)))
    (n : ℕ) (hsep : Mono (kernel.ι b.hom ≫ formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) Q.obj))
    (M : CoherentFormalModule X J) (f g : M ⟶ (completion X J).obj Q)
    (hcomp : f ≫ (completion X J).map b = g ≫ (completion X J).map b)
    (hlevel : f.hom.app (op n) = g.hom.app (op n)) : f = g
